title: interleaved-release-conduct-framework-wip
body:
Purpose:
This is a sticky working doc for an 'interleaved release' approach — mix small canaries (safety-focused) with concurrent A/B exposure windows (metric-driven) so we can validate both safety signals and product-level value in parallel without overloading infra or creating noisy signal contamination. Target audience: rollout stewards, SRE oncall, product owners, data science, solutions eng.

Context / motivation:
- Traditional canary then AB is slow for LLM features where behavior drift and cost interplay matter (model variant A reduces cost but may change calibration).
- We need a practical way to run safety-first micro-canaries (1%) and short-duration AB windows (5–10%) that are orthogonalized and instrumented to avoid cross-contamination.
- Must preserve latency SLOs and capacity planning for Dedicated customers.

High-level flow (phases):
1) PREP (day -7 to 0): final model artifacts, canary config, AB hypothesis, evaluation prompt set (small, curated), synthetic traffic scripts. Confirm infra capacity reservations for burst and degradation fallback lanes.
2) SAFETY CANARY (hours 0–6): 0.5%–1% traffic, blunt safety checks only (hallucination heuristics, toxicity filters, authz). Short TTL, manually reviewed hits for edge cases. No product metric evaluation.
3) ORTHOGONAL AB WINDOW (hours 6–24): 5% traffic split for A/B variants (A=control, B=feature). Observability focused on customer-visible metrics (engagement, conversion proxy), costs, and latency. Use timebox windows (12h) and stagger cohorts to avoid diurnal bias.
4) STAGGERED RAMP (day 1–7): Increase exposure gradually if both safety and AB signals are green. Use cohort rotation: day1 internal + beta customers, day2 small public cohort, day3 wider.
5) FALLOVER & FALLBACK (any time): automatic fallback to pinned model variant when critical thresholds breached.

Roles and stewarding:
- Release Steward (owner): coordinates sequence, signs off PREP. (typical: Product PM)
- Safety Lead: reviews safety canary outputs & triages.
- Data Lead: defines AB metrics, sets dashboards and hypothesis.
- SRE/Capacity: reserves capacity, monitors latency/cpu/gpu queues, manages fallback lanes.
- Communications owner: socializes changes and postmortem notes.

Orthogonalization techniques (key idea):
- Time-based separation: safety canary first, AB windows after a short cooling period to avoid data cross-contamination in logs and metrics.
- User cohort isolation: pick independent user segments (by region/account-age/product-tier) for canary vs AB where possible.
- Synthetic traffic tagging: tag synthetic test requests so they are excluded from AB metrics and learning pipelines.
- Log partitioning: ensure tracing/span IDs for canary requests are labelled and not folded into aggregated dashboards.

Signal definitions and thresholds (initial defaults — calibrated by product):
- Latency: p95 token latency increase > 15% over baseline => alert P1, halt ramp.
- Error rate: 5xx or decodes failing > 1% absolute increase => revert.
- Safety score (automated heuristics): weighted safety metric drop > 10% on canary set => manual stop.
- Quality/regression: evaluation prompt pass-rate drop of > 5 percentage points on curated prompt suite => hold and triage.
- Cost: cost-per-1k-tokens increase > 25% relative to baseline for Dedicated customers => notify finance & opt to limit exposure.
- Product lift (AB): primary KPI uplift < minimal detectable effect (MDE) after 12h window => iterate or close experiment.

Instrumentation checklist (must be in place before PREP signoff):
- Per-route token-level latency and cost breakdowns (tokenization, decode, postprocessing).
- Signal labels for canary vs AB vs synthetic traffic.
- Eval harness: 200 prompt suite with known golden labels and meta tags.
- Alerting: on-call playbook, runbook links, and a dead-man timer if manual approval is not received within 2h of alert.
- Traces: sampled traces linked to request ids with model variant & kernel selection metadata.

Operational patterns and heuristics:
- Short AB windows (12h) reduce temporal drift and exposure time while enabling product signal collection.
- Use staggered cohort activation (shift start times across geos) to detect time-of-day confounds.
- Prefer 'canary-first' for any model change where safety or hallucination risk is unknown.
- If canary shows noisy signal due to low volume, run a second targeted canary (increase to 2%) rather than immediately escalating.
- For cost-focused rollouts (quantization/precision changes), prioritize Dedicated customers in the early ramp so we can measure unit economics under committed capacity.

Automation suggestions (todo backlog):
- A pipeline that takes a release descriptor and generates: traffic slices, synthetic tags, dashboards, and a pre-populated runbook checklist. (JIRA: ROLL-3421)
- Automated orthogonalization utility to reserve disjoint user cohorts across slices (region + account-age).
- Canary artifact store that keeps last 5 canary runs for quick diffing of top-k failure traces.

Comms templates (short):
- Pre-launch blurb (for #rollouts-ops): "Planned interleaved release: model v3.1.2. Safety canary 0.5% @ 10:00 PT, AB window 10:30–22:30 PT (5% split). Steward: Asha. Links: {confluence} {jira}. Ping if you see p95 > baseline+15%."
- Incident blurb: "Rollout pause: model v3.1.2 halted at 11:13 PT due to p95 token latency +21%. Steering to fallback variant v3.1.1. Oncall: SRE paged. Postmortem booked: ROLL-3421."

Escalation path and triage playbook (short):
1) Pager fires for threshold breach.
2) Oncall toggles traffic to fallback lane (automated toggle preferred).
3) Safety lead and data lead join with release steward within 15m.
4) Decide: immediate rollback vs pause + targeted probe.
5) Communicate to stakeholders and stand up war room if >30m.

Open questions / experiments to run:
- MDE sizing: what is realistic MDE for short 12h AB windows on our primary KPI? run retrospective simulations on last 6 months of metrics.
- Cache priming cost: how much synthetic traffic do we need to warm KV caches for low-latency LLM features without skewing product metrics?
- Orthogonality limits: when does user cohort isolation break (small customers, global accounts that cross segments)?

Immediate next steps (owner: Asha):
- Finalize the 200-prompt eval suite with DS (due EOD Fri).
- Spin up synthetic traffic generator with tagging (dev sprint ticket).
- Run a dry-run internal canary using playground traffic next Wed.

Notes to self / informal thoughts:
- Consider a "safety rolling window" metric: combine toxicity + hallucination heuristics with a variance estimator to avoid overreacting to single spikes.
- For multimodal features, treat image-heavy cohorts as separate cohort dimension (otherwise AB signal gets overwhelmed).
- Keep AB windows short but repeatable: 12h x 3 cycles beats 36h single window for catching intermittent regressions.

summary: Working scratchpad: propose a structured 'interleaved release' pattern combining safety canaries + orthogonal A/B windows. Draft contains phases, roles, instrumentation checklist, thresholds, automation ideas, comms templates, and next steps.
